ledger_scope: Flagged material claims and ambiguities, after reading all six held-out summary/synthesis outputs against supplied sources. Supported content is described through coverage and review notes; not an exhaustive standardized atomic-claim denominator.
annotation_limits: Qualification loss, event contradiction, citation drift, attribution and ambiguity remain distinct. Flag counts are not independent false-fact totals or comparable precision percentages.
configuration_review: Selected memory configuration:32K context, F16KV, explicit 1024MiB RAM prompt-cache limit. Default 8192MiB cache caused guard failures at 32K and 16K as old prompt states accumulated. This run completed all 12 requests normally, with full-source prompt 13916, output allowance 2048, margin 256. The selection addresses measured memory overhead, not a preference for a more favorable quality score.
citation_review: Fifteen stated answers have supported page sets; H2-Q1 page supports the core death but not the added killer identity. H1-Q1 quotation is reordered despite correct identity/page. Direct H3 summary has no citations. Synthesis newly assigns all H3 statements to 169, a wrong-page pattern. H4 domains belong on 360 rather than 359; territorial gains 361–362; Serb-Magyar friction 363; vision/revolt 365 rather than 363; urban decline 366; Thessalonica/Florence 367 rather than 366. Full-control Florence belongs on 367 rather than 366.
supported_content_review: Direct H1 preserves almost exterminated Alans, source geography, troop/death numbers and old Roman lines. H3 retains both administrative disgrace and surprise qualification rather than exonerating the state. H4 keeps by 1421 and sourceJohnVI, and 1425 is supported by 1422 plus three years. The independent control’s preference for Roman refuge over Hunnic surrender is compatible with the stated actions; unlike the direct/merged claim, it does not assert Roman enslavement.
synthesis_review: Merged H1/H2 are condensed, dropping the Corippus last-author flag but propagating other parent errors. H3 largely copies its parent while inventing page 169 citations; H4 copies its parent. All outputs stop normally without hitting 2048 tokens. Full control devotes three paragraphs to H1, omits H3 entirely, compresses H2/H4 into the last paragraph, and introduces four new clear error families, including a decisive Ad Salices despite its own correct extraction answer.
